- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.5) — model is overly optimistic in such contexts.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model lags in adjusting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns sharply negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves, failing to recognize momentum decay.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile or bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to err on the high side — treat such periods as “cautious” and reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model may overfit recent trends — apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overconfidence.
